title: Congressional participation in administering the law
shortTitle: Congressional participation in administering the law
summary: Congress can create and constrain agencies by legislation, but constitutional limits restrict its own participation in appointment, removal, and execution.
notes:
Buckley prevents congressional appointees from exercising significant administrative or enforcement powers. Bowsher rejects executive duties for an officer subject to congressional removal outside impeachment. Chadha’s opening note identifies bicameralism and presentment as limits on legislative vetoes. Myers also involved a statutory Senate role in removal.

Morrison distinguishes a law that limits executive removal while leaving removal in executive hands from a scheme that reserves power for Congress itself. The distinction helps separate congressional regulation through enacted law from congressional execution through retained institutional control. Ordinary oversight and information gathering can remain permissible even when Congress cannot exercise the operative administrative power.
